Subject: Infra route & compliance qualification — post-demo follow-up

Hi Sara / Jordan,

Great demo earlier — thanks for the candid product questions and the walkthrough of where Mediserve stores and processes PHI today. Per our call, wanted to capture a short recap and the decision levers that will determine the right hosting path for your use case: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC / on-prem).

Summary of what we heard from you:
- Use case: real-time patient note summarization and retrieval for care teams; PHI in input/output.
- Must-haves: BAA in place, customer audit rights for select logs, data residency in us-east, and SOC 2 evidence for our infra controls.
- Timeline: aiming for pilot in Nov, production in Jan.

Tradeoffs & initial recommendation:
- Hosted API (fastest): lowest time-to-prod; we provide BAA + SOC2 report; good if you accept redacted logs and our hosted encryption controls.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): predictable throughput and data isolation within our infra; supports customer-specific retention policies and more granular token-level cost visibility.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): highest isolation and control (suitable for strict audit or on-prem constraints) but longer ops lead time (~6-12 weeks depending on environment & approvals).

Asks / next steps for you (quick answers will help us size the right path):
1) Will Mediserve require an on-site SOC 2 audit or will a Redwood SOC 2 Type II report + artifact package satisfy auditors?
2) Do you need inbound integrations to stay within your VPC (we can support VPC peering / private link for Dedicated & Private)?
3) Will any downstream systems require tokens or logs to be retained beyond 365 days?

We’ve attached a draft BAA (BAA_template_v2.docx) and a short SOC2 summary (SOC2-summary-2026.pdf) to start — happy to redline the BAA for your legal team. If it helps, we can set up a 30-min compliance call with Laura (our compliance lead) and Rishi (solutions engineering) later this week.

Proposed immediate next step: can you confirm answers to 1–3 above and share a preferred 30-min window for a compliance/ops call?

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference

Hi all — quick answers below. Happy to jump on the compliance call if needed.

1) SOC2 + artifacts: Yes — Redwood provides a SOC 2 Type II report (we’ve attached a short summary) and we can produce an artifacts package on request. Typical artifacts we can provide for customer audits: access control logs (redacted as needed), configuration snapshots, change logs for production deployments, patch records, and periodic penetration test summaries. SLA: standard request turnaround is 5–7 business days for packaged artifacts; expedited requests treated case-by-case.

2) PHI retention / debug logs by hosting mode:
- Hosted API: default debug logs are retained for 30 days and are redacted for PHI by default; retention and redaction settings are configurable on Dedicated and Private.
- Dedicated: we can configure retention windows (30/90/365 days) and disable PHI retention for your tenant; logs can be routed to your S3 (or equivalent) under a retention policy you control.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): no Redwood-hosted debug logs unless you opt-in; full control over retention and storage.

Recommended path for Mediserve (based on call): start on Dedicated capacity with PHI retention disabled + BAA in place for the pilot. That gives faster time-to-prod than on-prem while meeting your audit controls. If you require on-site auditability or strict air-gap controls, we can scope a Private deployment as the next phase.

Attachments & links: SOC2-summary-2026.pdf (attached), link to artifacts request form: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/soc2-2026-summary

Suggested next step: I can join a 30-min call Friday 09/17 at 10am PT to walk auditors through artifacts and answer specific legal questions. Karthik — can you confirm and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Laura Bennett
